gold_defects.description: `force_color=True` doesn't actually apply color because `execute()` replaces `self.style` and drops the `ROUTE`/`HIGHLIGHT` aliases, causing `AttributeError` in `apply_color()`.
gold_defects.original_comment_excerpt:
`--force-color` still doesn't force color properly.

`handle()` only checks `color.supports_color()`, so `force_color=True` doesn't actually color the aligned output. When coloring kicks in, `BaseCommand.execute()` replaces `self.style` and drops the `ROUTE`/`HIGHLIGHT` aliases added in `__init__()`. That leaves `apply_color()` raising an `AttributeError`.

Probably best to either stick with the base style roles or re-add the aliases after the base command handles color.

gold_defects.description: Comment notes that short aliases (-u, -p, -f) exist but are missing from docs, while nearby entries include them, making docs incomplete.
gold_defects.original_comment_excerpt: This command has short aliases (`-u`, `-p`, `-f`) but the docs only show the long forms. Nearby `django-admin-option` entries include the short aliases when they have them, so we should add them here too.

gold_defects.description: `nargs="*"` allows empty prefix list, and `if prefixes:` guard silently falls through to listing all URLs — surprising behavior for a filtering option.
gold_defects.original_comment_excerpt:
With `nargs="*"`, `listurls --prefix` accepts no prefixes at all. The `if prefixes:` guard just skips filtering, so the command ends up listing every single URL. For a filtering option, that's pretty surprising.

It'd be better to require at least one value. Something like `nargs="+"` would work. Or we could raise an error when `--prefix` is given empty.

gold_defects.description: Comment identifies that `BaseCommand.execute()` overwrites `self.style`, dropping command-local color aliases before they can be applied — a behavioral bug.
gold_defects.original_comment_excerpt:
Yes, that would fix it too, as long as the new roles are included in the palettes that `color_style()` uses.

The issue is that `BaseCommand.execute()` overwrites `self.style`, so the command-local aliases get dropped before color is applied. Adding the roles to the base style or re-adding the local aliases after the final style is selected both seem fine to me.

`AlterField` propagated type changes correctly when a transitive relation used `to_field` with the remote field name, but not when it used the accepted attname alias instead.
